findings.message: This round makes the tag_release service use the shared `Version` schema, which trims and refuses blank versions. The tool's own input still says `newVersion: z.string()`, and it has no `propose` check. In chat, the model's arguments are checked against that loose input, so `tagCard` shows the raw value (write-cards.ts:40). That means the card and the service still disagree. A blank tag gets a confirm card that can never succeed, and a padded tag shows text the service won't store. Fix: use `Version` for `newVersion` in the tool input too, so the gateway trims it before the card is built and refuses a blank one before any card appears.
findings.scenario: In chat, 'Tag RTK l2 as "   "' → a 'Re-tag RTK l2 as    ' card is shown → Re-tag fails with 'the release needs a version'. ' l2b ' shows the card text 'RTK l2 is now  l2b ' while 'l2b' is stored.

findings.message: Same-site path checks now exist twice with different rules. `inApp` (a regex, now used by chat-move) and `localPath` in apps/web/lib/local-path.ts (it parses the URL and compares origins) both decide whether a path stays on this site. They can disagree. For example, `localPath` accepts '/a b' and percent-encodes it, while `inApp` refuses it. Fix: build one on top of the other, or pick one rule for both.
findings.scenario: A path with a space or a non-ASCII character: `localPath('/x y')` → '/x%20y' (accepted); `inApp('/x y')` → false (refused).

findings.message: `tagRelease` updates `version` without checking whether the new version is already taken. When it is, the write hits the unique (project_id, version) constraint and comes back as a raw database error. `createRelease` refuses the same case with a clear message (line 181). Because the new version is now trimmed, a padded tag that used to be stored as a separate version now collides too. Fix: refuse with `${projectKey} already has a release ${newVersion}` when the version is taken.
findings.scenario: RTK has v1 and v2. tag_release { version: 'v2', newVersion: ' v1 ' } → a raw unique-violation error instead of 'RTK already has a release v1'.
